note: Two systems. home = Coventry City Council kerbside collection (checked 19 Nov 2026 on coventry.gov.uk). halls = Coventry University student accommodation (accommodation.coventry.ac.uk). Only status 'verified' rules appear in the game. 'needs_check' means the source does not settle it. Rules change, so check your local system before acting on a specific item.

home.reason: Drinks cups can't currently be recycled in Coventry, so they go in the green-lidded general waste bin.

halls.reason: The university page doesn't mention coffee cups. Check with your halls team.

home.reason: Boxes contaminated with pizza or grease can't be recycled in Coventry, so they go in general waste.

halls.reason: The halls page says cardboard, including pizza boxes, should be clean and dry, but doesn't say what to do with greasy ones. Check with your halls team.

home.reason: The council page doesn't say where a clean pizza box goes. Check the council site or the Your Rubbish app.

halls.reason: Cardboard, including pizza boxes, goes in the recycling bin, as long as it is clean and dry.

home.reason: Wash it first, then put it in the blue-lidded recycling bin.

halls.reason: The halls page lists plastic bottles and trays, but not yoghurt pots. Check with your halls team.

home.reason: Glass goes in the blue-lidded recycling bin. The council gives no rinse rule for jars, so rinse as a precaution.

halls.reason: Glass jars and bottles go in the recycling bin. Rinse them first to avoid smells and contamination.

home.reason: Not allowed in any household bin. Take them to a retailer collection point or the tip.

halls.reason: The university page doesn't mention batteries. Check with your halls team.

home.reason: Kitchen roll goes in the green-lidded general waste bin, or in home compost if you have it.

halls.reason: The halls page doesn't mention kitchen roll. It lists napkins as general waste, so it probably goes there too. Confirm with your halls team.

home.reason: Flatten it, then put it in the blue-lidded recycling bin.

halls.reason: Cardboard goes in the recycling bin, as long as it is clean and dry.

home.reason: Wash and squash it, then put it in the blue-lidded recycling bin.

halls.reason: Cans and tins go in the recycling bin, as long as they are clean and dry.

home.reason: Wash and squash it first, then put it in the blue-lidded recycling bin.

halls.reason: Plastic bottles go in the recycling bin, as long as they are clean and dry.

home.reason: Cling film can't be recycled because it tangles sorting machinery, so it goes in general waste.

halls.reason: Plastic film goes in the general waste bin.

home.reason: Crisp packets go in general waste. Some city collection points, including The Hub on Jordan Well and Coventry University, send them for recycling.

halls.reason: Crisp packets go in the general waste bin.

home.reason: Plastic bags can't go in the blue or brown bins. Use supermarket bag recycling, or reuse them.

halls.reason: Plastic bags go in the general waste bin.

home.reason: The council says bubble wrap can't currently be recycled, but doesn't name a bin. Check the council before deciding.

halls.reason: Bubblewrap goes in the general waste bin.

home.reason: Fruit and vegetable peelings go in the food waste caddy.

halls.reason: Peels and plate scrapings go in the food waste bin, not the general bin.

home.reason: Teabags go in the food waste caddy.

halls.reason: Teabags and coffee grounds go in the food waste bin.

home.reason: Meat and fish, including bones, go in the food waste caddy.

halls.reason: Bones go in the food waste bin.

home.reason: The council pages disagree on hard plastic trays: one says the blue bin, the other says the tip. Check the council before deciding.

halls.reason: Plastic trays go in the recycling bin, as long as they are clean and dry.

home.reason: Vapes go to the tip, not in household bins.

halls.reason: The university page doesn't mention vapes. Check with your halls team.

halls.reason: Cardboard goes in the recycling bin, as long as it is clean and dry. Flatten it first.
